label: context.reference
text:
Operate the intended Unity Editor through the bound MCP Application. Read the current catalog and relevant Editor, scene or asset observations to choose an operation. Use actual returned identities and schemas; example tool names and remembered server behavior can be outdated.

For a complex change, trace how the affected scripts, assets and scene objects work together. Reuse the existing implementation where it fits. Keep dependent operations ordered and batch independent edits when the server supports them. Compilation or domain reload can change readiness and identities; continue from fresh results rather than repeating an uncertain edit.

Check the behavior the change was meant to produce. A script edit may need compilation and a relevant test; a scene change may need saved state or a visual observation; an asynchronous build needs its final job result. Choose the evidence that resolves the actual uncertainty and inspect related consumers when the result points beyond the first edited object.

Use only the granted connection and capabilities. Report concrete effects and remaining failures, preserving the distinction between a dispatched request and the Editor's completed result.
